angle: Who wrote 'Could only have been painted by a madman' across the sky of The Scream, and was it true?
hooks: The Scream has an insult hidden in its sky. Munch wrote it himself.
The figure in The Scream is probably not screaming at all.

script.text: Someone pencilled an insult into the sky of The Scream.
Munch painted it in Oslo in 1893.
script.say: Munk painted it in Oslo in eighteen ninety-three.

script.text: The faint line reads: Could only have been painted by a madman.
For decades, people blamed a visitor.
But infrared shows it sits on top of the paint, in Munch's own handwriting.
script.say: But infrared shows it sits on top of the paint, in Munk's own handwriting.

script.text: He wrote it after a medical student publicly questioned his sanity.
His own sister was committed to an asylum.
Yet the scene itself was real.
In 1892, he described a sunset walk when the sky turned blood red.
script.say: In eighteen ninety-two, he described a sunset walk when the sky turned blood red.

script.text: I felt a great, unending scream piercing through nature.
So the figure may not be screaming, but shutting the scream out.
Some blame ash from Krakatoa; others, rare mother-of-pearl clouds.
Even the white spots blamed on birds are wax from his candle.
Now his 1910 version is fading: its yellow is breaking into white crystals.
script.say: Now his nineteen-ten version is fading: its yellow is breaking into white crystals.

script.text: The cause is damp air, including the breath of visitors.
The madman's sky was real. What is wearing it away is us.

post.caption:
Someone wrote 'Could only have been painted by a madman' in the sky of The Scream. Infrared finally showed whose hand it was.
Would you have written it on your own painting?
